scope: Compound linker-n forms and invalid regular-noun alternatives
findings: All 16 paired surfaces accept with explicit regular noun roots: both correct compound forms and incorrect ordinary-noun alternatives.
Existing production zeytinyağı/yeryüzü roots accept zeytinyağıya/zeytinyağıda/yeryüzüye/yeryüzüdeki as well as correct n-linked forms.
Missing gökyüzü/başucu/hanımeli roots explain tested production rejection; simply adding them as regular nouns would introduce acceptance of incorrect gökyüzüdeki/başucudaki/hanımelideki too.
rejected_hypothesis: A generic inability to generate linker-n forms is not supported: explicit regular noun automata accept the correct surfaces, possibly via alternative possessive parses. Exact analyses were not traced.
classification: Compound class overgeneration and limits of root-only fix; no false claim correct n-linked surfaces are uniformly rejected.
limits: Invalid paired surfaces were morphology probes, not observed automatic outputs from correct inputs.
The two changed words belong to already observed missing-root family.
validation: Two targeted tests and 16 isolated acceptance checks passed.
next_step: Enumerate exact accepted analyses for compound forms if needed; do not implement root-only workaround without grammatical constraints.
